correctness.rationale: The equality of radical and the path span follows from the vertex semisimple quotient and acyclicity. The disjoint source-target idempotents give a single sandwich for any radical element if no two arrows compose. Otherwise, a genuine algebra quotient to T_3(K) yields the rank-two contradiction for the arrow sum. The finite-field deficit counts two independent nonzero arrow coordinates and is attained exactly in A_3. The explicit factors for both cases of ac=0 verify the converse. Standard-library exhaustive checks on two binary quivers and finite coefficient counts reproduce boundary cases; the algebraic proof establishes the unbounded claims.

value.rationale: The witness set Z_i(KQ) and the Jacobson radical are intrinsic algebraic invariants, and additive closure of Z_i is a substantive stronger property than each path individually admitting a sandwich representation. The theorem completely classifies when those invariants coincide over all finite acyclic quivers. The sharp finite-field deficit provides a quantitative obstruction with a natural minimal extremal instance and can inform probability of witnessing via zero-product sandwiches. It is not a mere restatement of Z_i spanning the radical or a single cheap negative example.
